pack.description: Phrasal verbs and conversational idioms heard in campus conversations, useful for Listen and Choose a Response and for natural spoken answers.
pack.selection_note: Internal high-yield selection of phrasal verbs and idioms common in everyday campus speech; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: to find the answer to something or understand it by thinking
entries.example_academic: Engineers eventually figured out why the bridge vibrated in high winds.
entries.example_spoken: I can't figure out how to submit this form.

entries.definition: to give a piece of work to the person who asked for it
entries.example_academic: Participants who turned in incomplete questionnaires were excluded from the analysis.
entries.example_spoken: Did you turn in your essay yet?

entries.definition: to give something, such as homework or a form, to a person in authority
entries.example_academic: Candidates must hand in all notes before leaving the examination room.
entries.example_spoken: I handed in the wrong file by mistake.

entries.definition: to leave a course, school or competition before finishing it
entries.example_academic: Students from low-income families are more likely to drop out in the first year.
entries.example_spoken: He dropped out of college to start a company.

entries.definition: to reach the same level as others after being behind; or to do work that should have been done earlier
entries.example_academic: Wages in the region have not caught up with those of the capital.
entries.example_spoken: I need the weekend to catch up on reading.

entries.definition: to fail to keep the same speed or level as others
entries.example_academic: Countries that neglected education fell behind their neighbors.
entries.example_spoken: If you skip two classes, you'll fall behind fast.

entries.definition: to put your name on a list in order to take part in something
entries.example_academic: More than two thousand volunteers signed up for the trial.
entries.example_spoken: I signed up for the yoga class on Tuesdays.

entries.definition: to try to find out the facts about a problem or situation
entries.example_academic: A committee was appointed to look into the causes of the accident.
entries.example_spoken: I'll look into it and email you tomorrow.

entries.definition: to think of an idea, plan or answer
entries.example_academic: The team came up with a cheaper way of purifying the water.
entries.example_spoken: We need to come up with a topic by Friday.

entries.definition: to delay doing something until a later time
entries.example_academic: The government put off the reform until after the election.
entries.example_spoken: I keep putting off my dentist appointment.

entries.definition: to use all of something so that none is left
entries.translation_fr: manquer de, ne plus avoir de
entries.example_academic: The expedition ran out of supplies two weeks before reaching the coast.
entries.example_spoken: We ran out of time before the last question.

entries.definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
entries.example_academic: Employees who get along with their supervisors report less stress.
entries.example_spoken: Do you get along with your new roommate?

entries.definition: to feel happy and excited about something that is going to happen
entries.example_academic: The delegates looked forward to a more open discussion on the second day.
entries.example_spoken: I'm really looking forward to the break.

entries.definition: to get information about something, or to learn a fact for the first time
entries.example_academic: The survey was designed to find out how residents use the park.
entries.example_spoken: I just found out that the exam was moved.

entries.definition: to stop trying to do something, or to stop doing something you did regularly
entries.example_academic: Many farmers gave up growing cotton when prices collapsed.
entries.example_spoken: Don't give up; you're almost done.

entries.definition: to tell someone a fact that they had not noticed or thought about
entries.example_academic: Critics pointed out that the sample included no rural schools.
entries.example_spoken: She pointed out two mistakes in my slides.

entries.definition: to arrange, organize or start something
entries.example_academic: The foundation set up a fund to support young researchers.
entries.example_spoken: Can you help me set up the projector?

entries.definition: to collect someone or something; or to learn something without formal study
entries.example_academic: Children pick up the sounds of a second language more easily than adults.
entries.example_spoken: I'll pick up the books from the library on my way.

entries.definition: to take someone or something to a place and leave them there; or to become less
entries.example_academic: Attendance drops off sharply after the first month of the program.
entries.example_spoken: Could you drop off my form at the office?

entries.definition: to arrive at a place, especially when expected
entries.example_academic: Only half of the registered voters showed up at the polls.
entries.example_spoken: He showed up twenty minutes late, as usual.

entries.definition: to find the answer to something by thinking; to develop in a good way; or to exercise
entries.translation_fr: résoudre ; bien se passer ; faire de l'exercice
entries.example_academic: Astronomers worked out the comet's orbit from three observations.
entries.example_spoken: Don't worry, everything will work out.

entries.definition: to check or study something carefully from beginning to end
entries.example_academic: The editors went over the manuscript line by line.
entries.example_spoken: Let's go over the answers before we hand it in.

entries.definition: to refuse an offer or request; or to make sound or heat lower
entries.example_academic: The council turned down the application to build on the wetland.
entries.example_spoken: She turned down the job because it was too far away.

entries.definition: to start talking about a subject
entries.example_academic: Several members brought up the question of cost at the meeting.
entries.example_spoken: Don't bring up the deadline; he's already stressed.

entries.definition: to decide that a planned event will not happen
entries.example_academic: The organizers called off the conference because of the storm.
entries.example_spoken: They called off the game because of the rain.

entries.definition: to move or progress at the same speed as someone or something
entries.translation_fr: suivre le rythme de, se tenir au courant de
entries.example_academic: Supply could not keep up with the growth in demand.
entries.example_spoken: I can't keep up with all the reading for this class.

entries.definition: to do something that corrects or balances a bad situation
entries.example_academic: Higher exports made up for the fall in domestic sales.
entries.example_spoken: I'll work on Sunday to make up for missing Friday.

entries.definition: to borrow a book from a library; to look at something that seems interesting; or to pay and leave
entries.translation_fr: emprunter ; jeter un œil à ; régler et partir
entries.example_academic: Readers may check out up to ten items at a time.
entries.example_spoken: You should check out the new café on Main Street.

entries.definition: to write the necessary information on a form
entries.example_academic: Applicants must fill out a separate form for each grant.
entries.example_spoken: I had to fill out three forms to change my address.

entries.definition: to spend time relaxing, often with friends
entries.example_academic: Teenagers in the study preferred to hang out in public spaces rather than at home.
entries.example_spoken: We usually hang out at the student center after class.

entries.definition: to take action in order to solve a problem; or to be about a subject
entries.example_academic: The second chapter deals with the origins of the conflict.
entries.example_spoken: I'll deal with the booking if you send the emails.

entries.definition: to do a task, plan or study
entries.example_academic: The survey was carried out over a period of six months.
entries.example_spoken: We carried out the experiment twice to be sure.

entries.definition: to experience a difficult period; or to look at something carefully from start to finish
entries.example_academic: The industry went through a period of rapid consolidation.
entries.example_spoken: Let's go through the checklist one more time.

entries.definition: to accept a job or responsibility; or to begin to have a quality
entries.translation_fr: accepter, se charger de ; prendre (un aspect)
entries.example_academic: The state took on responsibilities once left to the church.
entries.example_spoken: I can't take on another project this month.

entries.definition: to reduce the amount of something that you use or spend
entries.example_academic: Households cut back on meat when prices rose.
entries.example_spoken: I'm trying to cut back on coffee.

entries.definition: to finally be in a place or situation that was not planned
entries.example_academic: Much of the plastic ends up in the ocean.
entries.example_spoken: We ended up studying until two in the morning.

entries.definition: to find or meet something or someone by chance; or to give a particular impression
entries.example_academic: Researchers came across the letters while cataloguing another collection.
entries.example_spoken: I came across a great article for our project.

entries.definition: to meet someone by chance; or to begin to experience a difficulty
entries.example_academic: The project ran into difficulties when funding was cut.
entries.example_spoken: I ran into our old professor at the supermarket.

entries.definition: to trust someone to do something, or to expect something to happen
entries.example_academic: Farmers could no longer count on regular rainfall.
entries.example_spoken: You can count on me to bring the slides.

entries.definition: to recover from an illness, a shock or a disappointment
entries.example_academic: The economy took almost a decade to get over the crisis.
entries.example_spoken: It took me a week to get over that cold.

entries.definition: something that is very easy to do
entries.example_academic: For experienced translators, the first passage was a piece of cake.
entries.example_spoken: The quiz was a piece of cake; I finished in ten minutes.

entries.definition: feeling slightly ill
entries.example_academic: Several players were under the weather, which may explain the team's poor result.
entries.example_spoken: I'm feeling a bit under the weather, so I'll stay home.

entries.definition: having the same understanding of a situation or plan
entries.example_academic: The two agencies were not on the same page about who should lead the response.
entries.example_spoken: Let's meet quickly so we're all on the same page.

entries.definition: to decide to stop working on something for now
entries.example_academic: After twelve hours of negotiation, the delegates called it a day.
entries.example_spoken: We've done enough; let's call it a day.

entries.definition: to watch someone or something carefully to make sure they are safe or to notice changes
entries.example_academic: Economists keep an eye on inventory levels for early signs of a slowdown.
entries.example_spoken: Can you keep an eye on my laptop for a minute?

entries.definition: to quickly improve a skill or your knowledge of something you learned before
entries.example_academic: New staff were asked to brush up on safety procedures before the inspection.
entries.example_spoken: I need to brush up on my statistics before the course starts.

entries.definition: to finally do something that you have intended to do for a long time
entries.translation_fr: trouver le temps de, finir par
entries.example_academic: The council never got around to repairing the oldest bridges.
entries.example_spoken: I still haven't got around to answering her email.

entries.definition: to reduce the number of possibilities or choices
entries.example_academic: Genetic testing narrowed down the possible causes to two.
entries.example_spoken: I've narrowed it down to two topics for my paper.

entries.definition: to start to suffer from an illness
entries.example_academic: Nearly a third of the crew came down with fever during the voyage.
entries.example_spoken: I think I'm coming down with the flu.

entries.definition: to fail to happen or to be completed, though it was planned
entries.example_academic: The merger fell through when regulators raised objections.
entries.example_spoken: Our trip fell through because nobody booked the tickets.

entries.definition: to solve small problems or disagreements before something can go ahead
entries.example_academic: The two sides met to iron out the remaining differences in the text.
entries.example_spoken: We still have a few details to iron out before the presentation.

entries.definition: to leave very little time to do something or arrive somewhere
entries.example_academic: The team cut it close, submitting the proposal minutes before the deadline.
entries.example_spoken: Leaving at eight is cutting it close; the exam starts at half past.

entries.definition: not yet decided or certain
entries.example_academic: The future of the program remained up in the air after the budget cuts.
entries.example_spoken: My summer plans are still up in the air.

entries.definition: to stay awake all night in order to study or finish work
entries.example_academic: Students who pull an all-nighter before an exam tend to recall less the next day.
entries.example_spoken: I pulled an all-nighter to finish the lab report.

entries.definition: unable to decide between two choices or opinions
entries.example_academic: Many voters were still on the fence a week before the election.
entries.example_spoken: I'm on the fence about taking that course.

entries.definition: to be the explanation for something; or to form a particular part of a total
entries.example_academic: Exports account for nearly half of the country's income.
entries.example_spoken: How do you account for the difference between the two results?

entries.definition: to decide that something is not possible or not suitable
entries.example_academic: The tests ruled out infection as the cause of the symptoms.
entries.example_spoken: We can rule out Friday; half the group is away.

entries.definition: to stop using or providing something gradually, in stages
entries.example_academic: The government plans to phase out coal power within fifteen years.
entries.example_spoken: They're phasing out paper forms next semester.

entries.definition: to have as its main or basic point
entries.example_academic: The dispute boils down to a disagreement over who owns the data.
entries.example_spoken: It all boils down to how much time we have.

entries.definition: to be as good as what was expected or promised
entries.example_academic: The new treatment failed to live up to the claims made for it.
entries.example_spoken: The movie didn't live up to the reviews.

entries.definition: to accept an unpleasant situation or person without complaining
entries.example_academic: Residents put up with the noise for months before complaining.
entries.example_spoken: I can't put up with that buzzing light anymore.

entries.definition: to have to deal with a difficulty or opposition
entries.example_academic: Reformers came up against strong resistance from landowners.
entries.example_spoken: We came up against a problem with the software.

entries.definition: to keep something, especially money or time, for a particular purpose; or to decide not to consider something for now
entries.example_academic: A portion of the budget was set aside for emergency repairs.
entries.example_spoken: Try to set aside an hour a day for reading.

entries.definition: to choose not to take part in something
entries.translation_fr: choisir de ne pas participer à, se retirer de
entries.example_academic: Employees may opt out of the pension plan at any time.
entries.example_spoken: Can I opt out of the group project and write an essay instead?

entries.definition: to include a particular fact or amount when you calculate or plan something
entries.example_academic: The estimate does not factor in the cost of training new staff.
entries.example_spoken: Did you factor in the time it takes to get there?

entries.definition: to direct all your attention toward one thing
entries.example_academic: Investigators zeroed in on a fault in the cooling system.
entries.example_spoken: Let's zero in on the two questions everyone got wrong.

entries.definition: to choose one person or thing from a group for special attention, praise or criticism
entries.example_academic: The report singles out transport as the fastest-growing source of emissions.
entries.example_spoken: The professor singled out her essay as the best in the class.

entries.definition: a small, visible part of a much larger problem
entries.example_academic: The reported cases are only the tip of the iceberg.
entries.example_spoken: Those two complaints are just the tip of the iceberg.

entries.definition: at the beginning again, because an earlier attempt failed
entries.example_academic: When the second trial failed, the researchers were back to square one.
entries.example_spoken: The file got deleted, so we're back to square one.

entries.definition: to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often lowering the quality
entries.example_academic: Contractors who cut corners on materials were later held responsible for the collapse.
entries.example_spoken: Don't cut corners on the references; she checks them.

entries.definition: to make more effort than is expected in order to achieve something
entries.translation_fr: faire un effort supplémentaire, en faire plus
entries.example_academic: Firms that go the extra mile for their customers tend to keep them.
entries.example_spoken: She really went the extra mile to help me with my application.

entries.definition: a practical and approximate way of doing or measuring something, based on experience
entries.example_academic: As a rule of thumb, a sample should be at least ten times the number of variables.
entries.example_spoken: My rule of thumb is two hours of study for every hour of class.

entries.definition: to learn how to do something, especially when it is not simple at first
entries.translation_fr: prendre le coup de main pour
entries.example_academic: New users generally get the hang of the software within a week.
entries.example_spoken: It took me a month to get the hang of the citation style.

entries.definition: a situation in which someone has to learn a lot in a short time
entries.example_academic: New recruits face a steep learning curve in their first six months.
entries.example_spoken: There's a steep learning curve in that class, but it gets easier.

entries.definition: to decide how to act as a situation develops instead of planning ahead
entries.example_academic: With no reliable forecast, the organizers had to play it by ear.
entries.example_spoken: I don't know when I'll finish; let's play it by ear.

entries.definition: the final problem in a series that makes a situation impossible to accept
entries.translation_fr: la goutte d'eau qui fait déborder le vase
entries.example_academic: The new tax was the last straw for merchants already burdened by tolls.
entries.example_spoken: The broken heater was the last straw; I'm moving out.

entries.definition: suddenly and unexpectedly
entries.example_academic: The announcement came out of the blue and surprised even senior officials.
entries.example_spoken: She called me out of the blue after two years.

entries.definition: to avoid talking about something unpleasant, or to say as little as possible about it
entries.example_academic: The official history glosses over the famine that followed the reform.
entries.example_spoken: He glossed over the fact that we're already a week late.

entries.definition: to depend completely on something
entries.example_academic: The success of the scheme hinges on the cooperation of local farmers.
entries.example_spoken: Everything hinges on whether we get the room.

entries.definition: to try hard to deal with or understand a difficult problem
entries.translation_fr: se débattre avec, être aux prises avec
entries.example_academic: Economists are still grappling with the causes of the slowdown.
entries.example_spoken: I've been grappling with this proof all week.

entries.definition: to develop or end in a particular way, especially successfully
entries.example_academic: Few of the early predictions about the technology panned out.
entries.example_spoken: The internship didn't pan out, so I'm looking again.

entries.definition: to think carefully about something for a long time before deciding
entries.example_academic: The board mulled over the proposal for several months before rejecting it.
entries.example_spoken: Give me the weekend to mull it over.

entries.definition: to avoid doing something because you are nervous or not confident
entries.example_academic: Earlier studies shied away from questions of responsibility.
entries.example_spoken: Don't shy away from asking questions in the seminar.

entries.definition: to keep something bad from happening for a time
entries.example_academic: Emergency loans staved off the collapse of the banking system.
entries.example_spoken: I ate a banana to stave off hunger until dinner.

entries.definition: something that has both good and bad effects
entries.example_academic: Cheap credit proved a double-edged sword for small farmers.
entries.example_spoken: Working from home is a double-edged sword: more freedom, less focus.

entries.definition: to argue about very small and unimportant differences
entries.translation_fr: couper les cheveux en quatre, chipoter
entries.example_academic: The reviewers accused the author of splitting hairs over terminology.
entries.example_spoken: Let's not split hairs; the two versions say the same thing.

entries.definition: very different from something
entries.example_academic: The final agreement was a far cry from the ambitious plan first proposed.
entries.example_spoken: This dorm is a far cry from my room at home.

entries.definition: an obvious problem that people avoid discussing
entries.translation_fr: le sujet tabou, le problème que tout le monde évite
entries.example_academic: Funding was the elephant in the room throughout the conference.
entries.example_spoken: Nobody mentioned the elephant in the room: half the team hadn't done anything.

entries.definition: what you would expect to happen, especially when it is not good
entries.example_academic: Delays of this kind are par for the course in large public projects.
entries.example_spoken: The printer's broken again, which is par for the course.

entries.definition: a request or task that is very difficult to carry out
entries.example_academic: Halving emissions within a decade is a tall order for any economy.
entries.example_spoken: Finishing by Monday is a tall order, but we'll try.
